Hmmm... I made this poem, I want some criticisms, and some feedback for it

I wonder what I think I missed from there

I would say it's really good, there are some places where I think you could utilize punctuation more, specifically maybe a question mark at line 4 to leave the reader hanging. The lack of commas combined with the syllabic imbalance make me read this very quickly, which works amazingly if that was your goal, but if it wasn't then I'd say add some pauses (commas, hyphens, or semicolons) and either break up your longer lines or merge your shorter ones.

Also, and this is completely personal preference, but I feel like it could've been much more concise and gotten the point across sooner without risking a loss of interest. The real question to ask is "was this poem meant to be read, or spoken?" And that should tell you what to focus on - if you want it to be spoken aloud, and you want it to be done a certain way, there should be more markers for the speaker so they can read it the way you intended. If the way it's read doesn't really matter to you, then I'd say it's pretty good right now as a skilled spoken word poet could take this and elevate it with the tools you've given them. If it's meant to be read, then I feel it could be trimmed a little to keep interest (people in general don't have great attention spans, especially not for poetry) and utilize a few more tools to guide the reader, especially punctuation and line breaks.

The last thing I'll say is poems are at their best when they break their own rules to deliver a message. There's a few points throughout where you go away from the rhyme scheme, which I think should be utilized more, utilized later on, and given more of a sense of direction.

Overall, though, good poem.

god, that’s a good one. i think good omens has influenced the way i put comedy into my work, a but. for prose itself? it’s hard to tell. my early fantasy series, notably eragon and wire of fire, were VERY formative, as was the warrior cats series and stuff like that. but i’ve noticed that recently i’ve developed a more mature style which at times is brief and direct and at other times more flower, saying the same things with more words. idk where i got that. i mean, piranesi, influences my descriptions of things i think. looking outside books, i think the magnus archives has had an incredible impact on how i write firsthand experiences and present backstory. but tbh i think im a big jigsaw puzzle of everything i’ve ever read or watched.
